name: Toast
description: Transient status message with tone, position, and auto-dismiss.

ariaRequirements: aria-atomic=true so the full message is announced
stays mounted as a live region; message swaps in/out
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-07-05 — beta→stable (fleet #16): renders a real <div role=status|alert> with aria-live/aria-atomic; role/politeness derive from tone (error/warning=assertive, else polite). Slide-in animation is guarded by @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){ transition:none }, so reducedMotion is honest. tone is optional at runtime (untinted, polite when omitted); the enum default 'info' is the nominal semantic default. Re-verified: axe + plays green in light/dark/forced-colors, 100% controls operable / 0 inert (duration EFFECT_EXEMPT — timing prop), AT snapshots refreshed 4 modes. 2026-05-26 origin: production behavior verified; required stories aligned with validate:components. 2026-07-03 (batch 4): Toaster (Tailwind duplicate host) deleted; providers/ToastProvider is the single imperative host forwarding tone/position.

forbiddenUse: mount two overlapping fixed <Toast /> instances yourself; use ToastStack (or the app ToastProvider) so concurrent messages stack instead of replacing each other.
rely on Toast for compliance acknowledgements (cookie consent, legal notices); it auto-dismisses — use AlertBanner or Modal.
use Toast for validation errors on a field; the message detaches from the input — use the field's error prop.
dense: transient auto-dismiss status (default 3000ms); tone success|error|warning|info, 6 positions, sm/md/lg; fire imperatively via useToast().showToast(message, {tone, duration, position})

usage.description: Toast is the transient "confirmation after action" surface: it appears, announces itself, and auto-dismisses. Most consumers never mount `<Toast />` directly — the app-root `ToastProvider` (`@/providers/ToastProvider`) owns the single live region and exposes the imperative API: `useToast()` returns `{ showToast }`, where `showToast(message: string, options?: number | { tone?: ToastTone; duration?: number; position?: ToastPosition })` accepts a bare duration in ms (legacy) or an options object (duration defaults to 3000). The element stays mounted as a live region and swaps the message in/out, so assistive tech reliably announces every toast; errors and warnings escalate to role=alert automatically.

bestPractices.description: Fire toasts via useToast().showToast — the provider is mounted once at the app shell and handles the live region, position, and dismissal.
Keep the message to one short sentence; the toast auto-dismisses and cannot be paused, so long copy will be cut off mid-read.
Pass tone so the filled icon carries the meaning alongside color (WCAG 1.4.1); error and warning announce assertively on their own.
Raise duration (e.g. 5000-6000ms) for messages the user may need to act on, like a network-retry notice.
Do not mount two <Toast /> instances side by side — the auto-dismiss timer is per instance but the announcement doubles in the AT queue.
Do not use Toast for persistent status, compliance acknowledgements, or anything the user must read — it disappears on its own. AlertBanner owns those.
Do not put field validation errors in a toast; the message detaches from the field it describes — use the input's error prop.

anatomy.name: LiveRegion
anatomy.description: The permanently mounted wrapper (role=status or role=alert, aria-atomic); visibility animates via opacity so the region never unmounts.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Filled tone glyph (aria-hidden; the tone is conveyed by the announcement role and message).

anatomy.name: Message
anatomy.description: Single-sentence status text; swapped in on show and cleared on hide to reset the live region.
